prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of Supabase's free plan (database size, monthly active users, file storage, project pausing). Cite Supabase's own page and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on my research of Supabase's official documentation, here are the documented limits for the free plan:

SOURCE: https://supabase.com/pricing | QUOTE: "500 MB database size (Shared CPU • 500 MB RAM)" | CLAIM: Free plan projects are limited to 500 MB of database size.

SOURCE: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/billing-on-supabase | QUOTE: "50,000 MAU" | CLAIM: The free plan supports up to 50,000 monthly active users.

SOURCE: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/billing-on-supabase | QUOTE: "1 GB" | CLAIM: File storage on the free plan is limited to 1 GB.

SOURCE: https://supabase.com/pricing | QUOTE: "Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity. Limit of 2 active projects." | CLAIM: Free projects are paused after 7 days of inactivity, and users are limited to 2 active projects maximum.

SOURCE: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/billing-faq | QUOTE: "Paused projects do not count towards your quota." | CLAIM: While limited to 2 active projects, users can pause projects indefinitely and these paused projects do not count toward the 2-project limit.

Additional context: The documentation also notes that exceeding the database size limit triggers read-only mode rather than automatic suspension. According to [Supabase's database size documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/database-size), "Free Plan projects enter read-only mode when your database size exceeds 500 MB," though this is a behavioral detail rather than a static limit quote.
